I’ll be bold and give the first negative review. This doesn’t mean I think the game is bad; it’s a pity steam doesn’t give the ability to give a mixed review. ***Please note that the "negatives" below aren't necessarily bad for everyone. This review is aimed to explain what type of game to expect. Positives: ✅great aesthetics (art animation music etc) ✅game concept of morph ball + twin stick is very good and just feels like a logical and effective combo ✅tight gameplay design that is simple to understand and is easy to get into. Also avoids getting overly messy and chaotic as many roguelikes can ✅overall sense of talent, love and polish emanates from the game and devs Negatives (I will use more words to explain each point) 💔Execution of certain design elements is questionable as of day 1. using halfpipes on enemies is too effective and easily undermines the twin stick shooting aspect. You can keep going on halfpipes to land on enemies to easily sidestep most of the strategy and skill of the game, and the game even rewards such an exploit by your kill chain freezing while in the air and also resetting the chain timer when landing on enemies, even if you didn’t kill them. You can breeze through harder difficulties this way as well, especially with certain abilities like temporary shield. 💔related to above point, the game overall rewards staying in ball too much. Harder difficulties introduce enemies that must be jumped on or collided for all enemy variations. Combine this with the fact that staying in ball is safer and is better for moving around the map, and much easier to maintain kill chain, and the game doesn’t really incentivize in any way to ever actually get out of ball and play the game as a twin stick shooter. It seems the ball mechanic should enhance the twin stick experience, and it does on first impressions, until you start to understand how powerful and safe stuff like spamming jump kills is…and then it feels like the ball system does more to undermine the twin stick experience than enhance it. A player must make a conscious choice to play against what the systems incentivize you to do in order to enjoy the twin stick experience and I think that’s a significant flaw. 💔barebones content. I believe there are 4 worlds and 4 bosses. The worlds introduce some new mechanics but don’t expect breadth and variety. The levels are the exact same layout every run. Almost no dialogue or lore. 4 difficulty levels of the same 4 worlds and that’s the end. 💔 guns feel samey. There’s a decent amount of guns, but somehow they end up feeling all functionally similar. Probably partially because functionally they ARE similar in that generally to kill an enemy, a player first ball-boosts into an enemy (this is how you get more ammo), then shoots them as in a shoot-punch/shotgun-melee combo in Halo. Basically the game incentivizes shooting from point-blank range. You can begin to understand how this can quickly undermine the feel of guns being functionally different even if they would be at a distance. 💔not particularly captivating for more hardcore arcade shooter nor roguelike fans. This is not really the type of roguelike experience that begets a player to sink hundreds of hours clearing additional difficulty modifiers, studying its depth, experimenting etc. it’s also not an arcade experience that will require dozens of hours to get the hardest difficulty clear. It’s more a light, casual experience that will probably take a more seasoned gamer anywhere from a few hours to a casual weekend grind to clear the hardest difficulty and then move onto something else. ————————— Overall my feelings on the game are mixed. It no doubt has a lot of love and care that’s obvious when you play it. There’s a solid foundation and some great ideas. It’s currently a quite barebones experience that I personally believe will cater more to a casual audience than hardcore twin stick and roguelike players. Casual gamers will love the kinetic feel, lighter difficulty, charming and satisfying vibe, and leniency of mechanics such as the very easy kill chain. More seasoned gamers with an eye for things like exploits and balancing of mechanics and such may harbor more critical thoughts about the game.

前言 最近最火的游戏无非是帕鲁，而为什么火，或多或少有宝可梦的原因，不过呢，我对宝可梦没啥感觉，反而重温起了童年的动画片数码宝贝和铁甲小宝，其中的丸子龙，想象看过的人很难忘记，口头禅就是是男人就该默默地。。。而在昨天就出了一款新游戏叫做：《进击的机甲球》，战斗方式很像丸子龙，既可以变身成球撞击敌人保护自己，还可以在不变身的时候拿着武器战斗，那就来看看今天的：“车轮滚滚”吧！ 游戏简介 《进击的机甲球》，你将化身成为一个机甲球，既然开高达机甲，同时还可以化身成为球体对敌人进行撞击。你将驾驶着全副武装的机甲，在这个世界展开狂暴轰炸，用你武力在敌人中开辟一条血路，突破一切敌人的防御，体验肾上腺素飙升的极致肉鸽战斗！ 新手教程与中心结合 在游戏中，一进去就是游戏的新手教程，各种弹药补充，撞击，技能释放，都会在这里进行演示，如果后面会是不会的话，可以再回来滚一边，进行输出一波。而走到尽头就是游戏中心，在这里可以进行各种武器库填充升级，让你的战力更胜一筹，而升级后所有的武器都可以在进入游戏后获得，如果没有提前升级，那就游戏就不会刷新这些新的道具。 武器库的三种属性 在游戏中一共可以获得三种属性，升级项目，能力以及武器，需要通过现金才能抽奖获取，每次抽奖必是没有获得道具，这大大解决了非酋的问题，让广大非酋玩家可以很好的融入游戏中。游戏中一共可以获得两种货币，探索币和现金，分别对应左上角头像的右下方的两种颜色的货币，其中探索币只能在游戏关卡中进行使用，通关或者死亡后，将一键清零，而现金则可以带出来外面对武器库属性进行升级，提升技能，解锁更多战力。 关卡中的资源补充站 游戏中，每个关卡对应有三波敌人，打完就可以前往下一个关卡，而在前往boss关卡前，则会进行一次能源补充，很好的补充我们机甲的状态，以及旁边的属性上限提升，需要花费大量的探索币才能将它提升到上限，个人尝试了大概需要4+6+8次提升，每次250探索币，只能说多肝几次就好了。 游戏的boss都很有趣 让我想到了之前玩马里奥奥德赛的那些boss，技能设计的很有趣，但是也不难通关，让玩家开心娱乐地打通关游戏，每个boss都有三条命，2次锁血的机会，那就意味着不能一次性将他们击杀，只能积攒弹药，然后找到机会开干。 游戏中目前不足 个人觉得观感不好的是，一开始进入游戏就是英文界面，而且就算切换到中文界面也还存在不少待汉化的地方，比如boss的名字以及对应属性的一些界面介绍等等，这些希望还是早点全部汉化完，方便玩家更好了解游戏的全貌，除此之外，其他方面，玩起来也是非常爽快。 总而言之 能够驾驶高达机甲进行战斗已经是梦想了，没想到还能在让机甲变成球体进行撞击，同时获取弹药，这也就是意味着，你将拥有无穷无尽的弹药，只要不爽，你甚至可以通过撞击来通关游戏，真的很符合游戏的名字，如同铁甲小宝在我心目中的车轮滚滚。 [code] [h1]欢迎关注 [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao]乱七芭蕉[/url][/b] 鉴赏家[/h1] 欢迎各路 [strike]肥宅、哲学家、LSP、绅士[/strike] 大神和小白加入我们：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao][b]乱七芭蕉[/b][/url] 一起分享乱七芭蕉的 [strike]福利资源[/strike] 游戏经验：[b]Q群774704264[/b] [/code]

《进击的机甲球》是一款带有肉鸽元素的双摇杆射击游戏，在游戏中我们将扮演一只骑着机甲的猫猫，运用自己手上的武器或者将自己变成“武器”去打败敌人。 游戏在玩法上似乎是参考了某只被称作“蓝色闪电”的刺猬，因为除了最基础的双摇杆射击外，我们还可以把自己与机甲缩成一个“球”去打击敌人，并造成一个冲撞伤害。在游玩时，游戏为了体现玩家可以变成“球”这个特性，很巧妙的将“球”形态攻击与枪械的子弹做了联动——冲撞击杀敌人可以掉落弹药补给，这也就意味着我们并不能一直勇往无前的突突突了。 游戏在手感上十分优秀，无论是使用枪械射击，还是“带球撞人”，都十分顺畅丝滑，再加上游戏在关卡设计上也存在着许多加速坡道，玩家在机甲与“球”形态之间来回切换，并且可以利用这些地形来打出许多精彩的操作。 游戏的肉鸽元素在于它的关卡设计，游戏中总共有三个大关卡，而每个大关卡又包含着三个小关。每当完成一个小关时可以获得抽卡机会，卡片可以让我们获得一项新技能或者提升我们的属性能力；而每完成一个大关卡我们则可以来到一个吧台出（安全屋），我们可以在此恢复状态或者给自己升级。 这款游戏在游玩时总是令我上头，无论是攻击动作、关卡排布还是背景音乐设计都属一流水平，整体难度也并不是很高，总体来说能称得上一个优秀的作品，但是至于这个售价，我个人还是推荐等[b]打折[/b]再入手吧。 [strike]“让妈妈骄傲吧，破坏球！”（有端联想）[/strike] [code] [h1]欢迎关注 [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao]乱七芭蕉[/url][/b] 鉴赏家[/h1] 欢迎各路 [strike]肥宅、哲学家、LSP、绅士[/strike] 大神和小白加入我们：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/luanqibajiao][b]乱七芭蕉[/b][/url] 一起分享乱七芭蕉的 [strike]福利资源[/strike] 游戏经验：[b]Q群774704264[/b] [/code]

[i]Go Mecha Ball[/i] left a good impression on me via the Steam Next Fest demo, seemingly promising as a fast, dynamic rogue-like with high quality presentation and a strong game play foundation. Unfortunately any and all possibilities for more mechanical depth or nuance are sent to the drain within a few hours of play. There's a total of 4 worlds, 3 stages each featuring 3 waves of enemies which culminate into the world's boss battle. It's simple but certainly serviceable until you realize the stages are the exact same structure and order every run. Even the waves are composed of the same enemies and compositions, with the only variety being offered by a difficultly modifier that adds buffs to the already existing enemies. If there's any other function to the difficultly modifier, there's no indication whatsoever. In fact, the game makes a strong effort not to communicate any specific information to the player, making decisions in the already nearly identical runs feel shallow. The stats differentiating the playable characters are completely abstract beyond the amount of HP they start with ("Power, Collision, Gun"). Upgrades and abilities are straight-forward enough to not be an issue, but weapons are also represented with abstract bars and very un-descriptive descriptions. There's not much separating one weapon's usage from another, aside from just being better or worse at dealing damage, how many bullets it shoots, and how far those bullets go. Being in the ball form itself is where the game is at its best- and most exploitable. Enemies and even bosses have a hard time touching you once you're airborne and it's awfully easy to combo off of them without much effort. It's a shame especially since most of this could be curbed with some tweaks and more informative explanations. But the absolute lack of variety between runs kills the game outright. I can comprehend no procedural generation, but no stage variants entirely is simply bizarre. [i]Go Mecha Ball[/i] definitely captures a pinball machine's fast, fun spirit. It's unfortunately not a pinball machine but a rogue-like lacking any replay-ability or variety. And it's also unfortunately twenty bucks instead of a quarter. TL;DR 5/10

游戏很好，只说个人感受： 1、视角有点难受，特别是第一次打第二还是第三大关的高台，就剩高台上一个敌人，我吹风四五次都上不去。一些高低差让球不能很爽的滚动，也可能游戏就是这么设计的（可能还是我菜）。 2、武器，能力，升级要素需要每局游戏开始前去扭蛋解锁。看下来东西不少，但目前没组合出无敌的build。只有量的提升，主要还是靠操作，不是成型了就乱杀的类型。 3、一开始地形周围有保护罩，球撞到边缘会停住，后面忽然一关保护罩消失，一下不习惯，基本都是摔死的。摔下去的机制是扣血后弹起，如果弹起你没回到地面上，再摔下去还会掉血。甚至有一局我掉到地形下面的空间，弹起后磕脑袋来回在地形下面弹跳扣血扣死。感觉可以设计成掉下去给你保护回地面上。不过问题不大。 4、枪械没有太大特色，数值区别也不明显，虽然枪械很多，但总的还是射速快的，射速慢的，喷子，狙击之类的。不知道是不是解锁太少了，希望有更多有意思的枪，不然一般我没有选枪械流派的想法。 最后，还是一款不错的游戏，主打一个操作弹球，操作难度不低，67不亏。

Mixing genres almost always results in an interesting outcome, but every once in a while it creates something that feels distinct from everything in the recipe, and a game is crafted that is more than the sum of its parts. Go Mecha Ball is one of those results. Abbreviated Review: https://youtu.be/6LOctI5wdZM [h1]Top-Down Pinbooter [/h1] It doesn’t feel like there are a lot of heavy hitters in the top-down shooter world these days. Maybe because they’ve all become auto-shooting Vampire Survivors clones. However, Go Mecha Ball takes that straightforward realm of mowing down enemies with guns and adds a layer of movement and environmental challenges that make it a much more thrilling experience. In addition to being able to slowly plod around wielding a swappable duo of guns that can vary from longer-range single-shot snipers to wedge-blasting shotguns, you can tuck yourself into a rolling ball Samus style and take off rolling at a higher rate of speed. This rolling mechanic allows you to move faster while also cruising up and down the vertical elements of three-dimensional levels via ramps, bounce pads, and even some glorified hamster tubes. These traversal features are both a convenient way to move around and dodge enemy attacks, but also a requirement to access some areas to attack enemies. Yet, the rolling mechanic has a much more aggressive component to it in that when you are going fast enough and hitting enemies, you will cause a significant amount of damage as well as disrupt many of their telegraphed attacks. In addition to that great offensive bonus, it’s also the only way you can generate ammo packs, which means it's just as much a requirement as a general benefit to you clearing the stage. When you combine the boon of bashing enemies as a ball and the environment’s numerous ramps, bumpers, speed boosts, lifting fans, and bounce pads that give you acceleration, you get an experience that crosses the visuals and movement of pinball with the tactical dodging and attacking of a top-down shooter. The combination works so well, it almost feels familiar even when I’ve never played a game like it. [h1]Visual Cacophony[/h1] Much like pinball, part of the challenge of the game is created by the assault of light and sound the game bombards you with. Things can and often do move very quickly and there are numerous times even in the early stages where you can lose track of what’s going on because of the speed and explosive effects. The more abilities you unlock, the more likely this is going to happen, and the enemies are quick to contribute. The audio joins in with a somewhat eclectic soundtrack that fits the ‘glitchy’ styling of the interface and some enemies. It will also fade away as you take damage giving you a slightly better idea of when ♥♥♥♥ is hitting the fan, because in the confusion it can occasionally be hard to tell. Yet, it all works together to create an experience that is as challenging as it is fun. Like a lot of roguelikes, the whole run can come down to having the right weapons or abilities, or the lack thereof, and will succeed or fail accordingly. Small mistakes can add up and if you get to a scenario where you don’t have health and the pre-boss stores aren’t selling it (or you don’t have enough for it) you might have a hard time making it to the end. I actually completed the game fairly early on and thought that it felt like a cakewalk, but when I bumped up to the first level of post-win difficulty, I lost like five consecutive runs up to and on the first boss. Then I went back to the base level of difficulty and lost five more. However, that seems like a fairly common experience for me in roguelikes. What makes the big difference is my will to continue playing the game. Go Mecha Ball kept me coming back when I won or lost. Even as the only real reward is spending accumulated currency on little gacha machines to unlock new abilities, weapons, and upgrades you’ll collect between each level from a random trio of selections. If there’s one fault I could notice, it’s that once you unlock the four total varieties of ‘mecha balls’ that whole unlocking mechanic shuts down. I kind of assumed you'd be able to continue upgrading them via that system and investing in making these higher difficulty settings a little more accessible. Yet, even with that issue and a couple of moments of big framerate loss when things got exceptionally “explodey,” this is an excellent game with tons of polish and replayability. I hope the future brings more levels, bosses, and content in every form, but even if it doesn’t, it’s an easy recommendation.

[quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote] [h1]《进击的机甲球》：机甲福瑞，三维弹球[/h1] [b] 前言 [/b] 《进击的机甲球》是一款上帝视角清版动作肉鸽游戏。游戏中，玩家需要驾驶一台可以变为球体冲撞敌人的机甲，在一张又一张布满机关令人眼花缭乱的地图中大杀四方。 只不过相较于一般的肉鸽游戏而言，本作过于快速的节奏和不易上手的冲撞手感，都使这部作品注定成为一道只适合尝鲜式游玩的预制快餐。 [b]过于自由的3D弹球[/b] 在本作中，玩家需要操控一只驾驶机甲的小猫，在一群外星机器人的包围下，扫荡一层又一层的关卡。 而作为一款上帝视角肉鸽游戏，玩家在本作中除了需要利用方向键控制角色移动、鼠标控制武器的射击方向外，这款游戏不同于同类作品的最大特色就是，玩家还可以通过长按鼠标右键，将主角缩成一个横冲直撞的铁球。 虽然在此状态下，玩家无法利用武器攻击，但你可以通过鼠标左键消耗体力值进行冲刺，被冲刺攻击到的敌人会在受到伤害的同时，掉落弹药箱，同时他们还有较小概率会掉落回血药。而在球体状态下，玩家不仅能够轻微增加移动速度，地图中也设置了很多专门为“弹球”准备的机关，你既可以利用这些机关来转移阵地、从而歼灭所有敌人，也可以利用这些机关大幅增加移动速度，甚至直接冲撞到敌人身上造成伤害。 即便玩家在游戏中无法主动跳跃，地图中大量的弹球机关也可以让你做到四处腾空。同时，由于在快节奏的战斗下，本作的核心玩法“冲刺”会有些难以掌握方向，因此初次接触本作的玩家，在彻底熟悉游戏之前，会对游戏机制感到一头雾水。 [b] 后记 [/b] 尽管作为一款肉鸽游戏，本作随着层数的递进会逐渐出现各种全新的地图机制与特殊敌人，再加上本作并没有局外升级，所有永久升级项目也全包含在游戏内，玩家可以掉落的技能与武器更是需要利用特殊货币在第一层中通过抽取来解锁，更不用提游戏中每一层都需要清扫三波敌人才可以通关的设计了。这也就导致不同玩家在本作的大部分不同关卡内，收获的游戏体验大同小异。 因此，即便本作玩法画面吸引人，玩法新颖，游戏手感十分爽快，但它也注定是一道肉鸽游戏中的预制快餐，只适合游戏荒时偶尔捡起来尝尝鲜，并不适合一口气打到通关。

游戏在画面上应用蓝红为主的配色，配合大量的灯光，营造出一种未来的霓虹世界。游戏中的机甲球实际上一个机甲机器人，走路挺有沉重感，机械力量强健。酷炫的机甲球、多变的场景、绚烂的光影等，让整个游戏看起来十分酷炫。游戏主角是一个机甲球，所以本作没有语音。游戏中的电子配乐很好听，音效也很酷，但是两者搭配起来却不尽人意，音效的旋律太像配乐了，结果就像是两个配乐混在一起，非常杂乱。 游戏的教程设计很精妙，当玩家登入游戏，来到平台，直接右拐就进入了教学关卡，一气呵成。整体教程设计中规中矩，基本上所有操作都讲得很清楚了。游戏本身的操作并不复杂，就是键盘移动，鼠标左键射击，右键翻滚，很容易上手。但是，游戏的技巧上限很高，在游戏后期，玩家需要一边躲闪潮水般的攻击，一边进行各种连击，快速节奏下很容易手忙脚乱。 游戏可以看作是一个快节奏的动作射击游戏，玩家将化身机甲球，去战胜各种敌人。枪支的射击手感不错，不同枪的后坐力完全不一样。随着游戏的进行，玩家可以获取不同的能力，例如扔出一对飞盘，对前方的敌人造成伤害；放出一道电磁脉冲，晕眩附近的敌人。攻击手段的多样性，让整个战斗过程非常爽快。 作为一个机甲球的主角，自然在速度上是很有优势。为了体验机甲球的急速效果，开发组在游戏里赋予了敌人的大量范围攻击，让玩家必须经常化身机甲球来进行走位。在游戏中，变身机甲球之后可以通过冲撞敌人来获取弹药。不仅如此，冲撞敌人还可以打断对方的攻击状态。有一说一，键盘移动和鼠标转向的配合，在高速下相准确命中目标，并不太容易。 游戏有着不少的肉鸽要素，最典型的就是关卡地形。在游戏中，每一关的地形都不相同，或是隧道穿梭，或是平台堆叠，或是长坡轨道。当然，非常适合机甲球的碗池地形，是每一关都必不可少的。而且，敌人的种类不少，有球形敌人横冲直撞，有炮台敌人不断发射炮弹，有柱子敌人不断发射激光，有飞行敌人不断骚扰……关卡中会随机刷新各类敌人，玩家需要采取不同的战术应对。笔者最为满意的是本作的BOSS战，不仅每一个BOSS的技能和打法都不一样，而且很多招式都逼迫玩家必须用机甲球的急速和碰撞来化解，打起来很有感觉。 游戏算得上是清版关卡制，必须清理完这个房间的所有敌人，才能进入下个房间。当清理完一个关卡内的所有敌人之后，就可以结算奖励。在这里，结算奖励是三选一，玩家可以从升级项目、能力等方面进行强化。这种经典的设计，可以让玩家在每一局游戏里都有不一样的体验。 游戏有两种代币，黄色的是局内代币，蓝色的是局外代币。前者可以在局内购买装备、升级能力等，后者则是解锁更多的武器、能力、升级项目的。游戏中总计20多种武器、20多能力、几十种，但玩家初期只能使用4种武器、4种能力、10种升级项目，剩下都要靠慢慢肝。 总体来看，本作算是一个非常不错的肉鸽动作射击游戏。不过目前流程较短，仅只有4大关卡4个BOSS，在深度上略有不足，希望后续能加强一下。 [h1][code] 欢迎关注：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42228259] 游话好说 [/url] 我们是一群游戏爱好者，希望能用评测来帮助大家认识更多好游戏，期待您的同行！ [/code] [/h1]

[h1]高速飙车，爽快冲击！[/h1] 《进击的机甲球》是一款高速肉鸽游戏，你将操作一个机甲球，用强大的火力将敌人击溃，或是翻滚起来狠狠撞碎敌人。赛博朋克风格的地图充满了霓虹元素，你可以通过坡道到处翻滚上上下下。丰富的移动方式，飙车一般的翻滚与冲撞，多种武器与能力，用眼花缭乱的操作击溃敌人吧！ [h2]肉鸽设计[/h2] 本作虽为肉鸽游戏，但肉鸽属性并不突出。在每次开局时，可以消耗游戏内积攒的代币来解锁全新的升级、能力和武器等，在局内有概率获取。每通过一个小关后，还可以从能力、升级等三选一。在游戏内我们可以装备两个武器进行切换，同时还可以装备两个能力，冷却结束后即可释放。每一场战斗将分为多个波次，全部结束后可以通过一个炫酷的传送门到达下一关。游戏共有四种机甲球可供选择。 [h2]战斗手感[/h2] 能扮演机甲球到处翻滚确实很爽，但是太容易受到敌人的各种攻击了，挫败感很强。每场战斗将刷出大量的敌人，还经常分布在不同的高低区域，翻滚时还需要找到正确的路径向上移动。冲撞时除了容易受到敌人攻击外，还需要瞄准好进行冲刺攻击。你还可以将敌人冲出战场直接击杀。冲撞击杀敌人后，可以获得弹药等，因此鼓励通过火力压血线后翻滚撞死敌人。手柄的操作体验也一般，辅助瞄准并不好用，需要使用双摇杆边移动边瞄准敌人攻击。 [h2]总结[/h2] 《进击的机甲球》扮演机甲球边翻滚边开枪的玩法设计非常有趣，上手有着十足的新鲜感，但是游玩过程中体验不佳，内容较少，肉鸽成长属性的设计也并不优秀，略有遗憾。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44066492//]来者不拒鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 做最真实的评测，用心玩家推荐 [/b][/u]

【6.8★】比快餐好点，这款是预制菜肉鸽，适合尝鲜不宜天天吃。 鸽子的肉质Q弹爽嫩，就好比游戏里的机甲球一样，一入口就在舌尖里弹来弹去，有自己的特色但味道还是差了点： 和小怪的战斗非常慢热无聊，它们都喜欢待在原地等你滚过去打它，要命的是每一关的地形小台阶非常多，某些小怪的位置需要来回弹来弹去才能到达，费时且麻烦，还有晕车风险。 倒是BOSS战设计得很不错，非常精彩刺激。我的建议是缩小关卡的活动区域，让小怪自动追踪玩家，加速每关的通过时间。把可以去除的且不影响自身风格的要素全去了，把爽的侧重点放在战斗碰撞上，这样游戏会好玩很多。 【优点】 ① 超强的打击感，把敌人创飞出去的时候真的非常爽。 ② 《蜘蛛侠平行宇宙》般的新潮美漫视觉特效，帅呆了。 ③ 一流的美术，不管是UI、枪械还是机甲设计都十分有特色。 【不足】 ① 首发优惠 67.49 ¥，现价 53.09 ¥，奶奶滴恶心首发玩家是吧。 ② 内容太少，一共就4关，关卡设计过于重复，通关后就不想再玩了。 ③ 关卡的地形设计明显是奔着爽去的，但是很难让玩家把控好，过于硬核，从第四关开始没有护栏后经常掉下去...... ④ 每关敌人太多，设计两波小怪就够了没必要拖延时间。 ⑤ 作为一款爽游，没必要加子弹限制，弹球撞击的冷却时间可以再改短些。 ⑥ 晕3D玩家建议把 镜头摇晃、屏幕闪烁和振动 调到最低，虽然是俯视角但镜头跟随弹球飞速运动，球弹来弹去镜头也跟着晃来晃去，打完一把差点没把我送走，加上强烈的光污染特效真的是催吐神器......

Okay, a marginal thumbs down for this mix of pinball combat and twin-stick shooting roguelite action. The good: Aesthetically pleasing. Bright and colorful, this is the kind of game you expect to find on the Switch. When you get into the zone ala Sonic, it's fun. Arenas are thoughtfully designed, for the most part. Bumping baddies off the map is the best. Good music. The meh: I wouldn't play this with a mouse and keyboard, and if you play with a controller, I hope you have a strong LEFT TRIGGER index finger, because you're going to pressing it almost *constantly* to keep you in ball mode. And this brings me to a very subjective complaint - the twin-stick shooter aspect is pretty minimal because you're always rolling and colliding as your primary attack. In fact when you slow down to shoot you're immediately a lot more vulnerable. I can't comment on performance, but my brand new gaming desktop 's fans started whirring, so if you're thinking of playing this on a potato, maybe think again. The bad: Okay, confession time, I'm old and pretty bad and my reflexes are probably getting worse by the day. But I've had a lot of fun with modern indie roguelites that don't play too rough. And I think this one plays a bit too rough in three departments. First, if you were hoping for difficulty levels, forget it. This is a one-size-fits-all kind of game. More egregiously, health regen is almost non-existent - at least I haven't experienced it in the two hours I've played so far. I played with the gun that's supposed to give you random health drops, and I didn't get a single one. This means that even if you get past the first 9 waves and defeat the first boss, you're most likely going to be unable to last more than a couple of minutes after that. There *is* a store you can access right before the first boss, but 4 out of 5 times I've been unable to afford anything (perhaps because of RNG?). And even if you are lucky enough to find a health recharge at said store, it's just a couple of HP - it doesn't refill your counter. Talk about stingy... The meta-progression is equally stingy. In two hours of play, I don't think I unlocked anything that gave me any advantage in subsequent games. And though there did seem to be unlocks to be had, there was no indication as to how I would be able to get them. The verdict: A lot of people seem to love this game, so it's obvious my opinion here is in the minority. And maybe slogging through another couple of hours might get me into the groove. But having gotten this in a twin-stick bundle, it just didn't fulfill my impulse to pew-pew the way I had hoped.

I really like the concept of this game. Which is why it's so painful for me to say it absolutely fumbles the execution, and I wouldn't be able to recommend it in good faith. It's advertised as a roguelite, despite the fact that it doesn't start feeling varied until you've gotten through a good chunk of what's this game's laughable idea of meta-progression: A Gacha Machine. Now, I don't know if the Gacha is actually RNG-based or not, but its presentation does nothing to tell me that it's not, so we'll work under the assumption that it is, considering I ended up getting things like basic fire-rate and damage upgrades way towards the end. Speaking of, the upgrades don't feel as substantial because you only get them as a reward for progressing through the "normal" wave-based combat levels. While I understand why the shop levels don't give you upgrades (although having more than a couple in stock would do wonders for the game's balance) I don't understand why the Bosses also lack an upgrade reward. More chances would make me more inclined towards grabbing lesser upgrades and not always gravitating towards the obviously all-around OP abilities or combos that knock over the whole balance of the game. And about balance... why are there barely any dynamic healing options? Sure, there's upgrades, but you'd expect there'd be some built-in healing mechanic that'd make it less of a critical choice to have to buy health refills at the shop (and it feels like them making it mandatory for health refills to appear in every shop in an update was just quick patchwork that doesn't solve much - or maybe they were workshopping something else that never came). Instead, there is a game-breaking glitch that makes it so you can refill your whole HP in the press of a button, that, once discovered, is more than just tempting to use considering how easy it is to replicate. I will not tell you about it in this review in case you're still considering buying the game, but I'm sure many other people can do so if need be. What I know is that the devs are allegedly aware of the issue and haven't bothered to patch their game for longer than a year now. The game, also, does not have any kind of functional key rebinding. When you assing a key or button to something else, if it had another previously assigned action which you moved somewhere else, it just does both things instead of the one you assigned. For example, rebinding an ability to the button with which you used to swap weapon makes it also swap your weapon when you use that ability, no matter if you changed the button with which you swap your weapon. This results in crazy hand cramps if you play for longer than an hour with the default controller bindings, especially because abilities can't even be swapped around, and will remain assigned to the same buttons in the order you got them first. In the topic of the game hurting you physically, there's also the audio glitches. First of all, the volume is ridiculously high from the beginning, blasting you with loud music that can't be changed until you go to the audio settings. Now, you'd expect your settings to remain saved for every following time you boot up the game... wrong! The volume won't change until you go back to the settings, which are SAVED, but the game won't remember until you open the menu itself, instantly shifting back to whatever you'd set before. Now, beyond the title screen, there's an audio glitch which will happen very frequently that loops the beginning of the sound effect for an enemy being defeated over and over, resulting on a loud rattling noise that won't go away until you finish the level you're on. I'm not asking for more content, but the game needs a severe rework of many systems so that the experience is more enjoyable than the slow grind that it is at the moment, and many bug fixes that address the many out-of-bounds, visual and unadjustable ear-shattering audio glitches that happen at every second. Because again, once you get all of the meta progression out of the way, the game is an absolute friggin spectacle to play AND watch, and an absolute show of skill. The gameplay loop is tremendously addicting, the combo system keeps you hooked and the arcade mode shows that very well. The character design is super cool, the music is banging, the setting is original and interesting... but it just misses the mark by feeling unfinished. This game is abandoned at the time of me writing this review. It's a big shame, because the good parts in it are really good. But the bad ones are a genuine dealbreaker.

Go Mecha Ball takes the familiar foundation of the roguelite twin-stick shooter and injects it with a level of speed and creativity that makes it feel refreshingly distinct. At its core is a clever mechanic that allows players to instantly transform between a combat-ready mech and a high-speed rolling ball. This transformation is much more than a visual gimmick, as it fundamentally changes how every battle is approached. Instead of simply dodging enemy attacks on foot, players can build momentum, launch themselves across arenas, ricochet off environmental objects, and crash directly into opponents before seamlessly switching back to unleash an arsenal of devastating weapons. The result is a game that rewards constant movement and aggressive play rather than cautious positioning. Combat remains the driving force throughout the adventure, delivering frantic encounters packed with enemy robots, explosive effects, and satisfying firepower. Every run offers access to an extensive collection of weapons and combat abilities that dramatically influence how battles unfold. Machine guns, explosive launchers, energy-based weapons, drones, and powerful special attacks can all be combined with passive upgrades to create highly personalized builds. Rather than locking players into a single strategy, the game encourages experimentation by presenting new upgrade combinations during every run. Discovering unexpected synergies between abilities becomes one of the most rewarding aspects of progression, giving each attempt a unique identity while maintaining the addictive "one more run" appeal that defines successful roguelites. Movement is where Go Mecha Ball truly separates itself from its contemporaries. The arenas are intentionally designed around physics-based traversal, transforming each battlefield into an obstacle course filled with ramps, giant fans, bounce pads, and other interactive elements. Mastering these features becomes just as important as mastering combat itself. Rolling through hazards, launching into the air, maintaining momentum around corners, and timing transformations correctly all contribute to a gameplay loop that constantly feels energetic. The environments are not simply decorative backdrops but integral components of every encounter, rewarding players who learn how to use the terrain to outmaneuver overwhelming enemy forces. The game's progression system provides substantial replay value through its selection of playable mechs and expansive upgrade options. Each mech possesses its own strengths, weapons, and abilities, encouraging players to adapt their tactics rather than relying on a single favorite approach. As new upgrades become available, players gain access to increasingly powerful combinations that can dramatically alter combat performance. Because upgrades appear in different combinations during each playthrough, no two runs feel exactly alike, and the unpredictability helps maintain excitement even after many hours of gameplay. This variety keeps experimentation at the forefront while ensuring that player skill remains equally important alongside progression. Visually, Go Mecha Ball embraces a colorful futuristic style that perfectly complements its arcade-inspired gameplay. Bright neon lighting, imaginative robotic enemies, and vibrant particle effects create an attractive presentation without sacrificing gameplay clarity. Even during the busiest firefights, important attacks and hazards remain visible, allowing players to react effectively despite the constant action. The four major worlds each feature distinctive visual themes and enemy types, preventing the environments from becoming repetitive while gradually introducing fresh challenges that keep the campaign engaging. Memorable boss encounters further enhance the experience by testing everything players have learned about movement, positioning, and build optimization. The audio design plays a significant role in maintaining the game's relentless pace. Sound effects deliver satisfying impact for every collision, weapon blast, and enemy explosion, while the energetic soundtrack dynamically complements the action unfolding on screen. The music reinforces the sensation of speed and momentum, making every successful chain of attacks and high-speed maneuver feel even more exhilarating. Combined with the game's responsive controls, the presentation consistently captures the excitement of fast-paced arcade action while remaining polished throughout. Although the game is welcoming enough for newcomers, its emphasis on speed and multitasking creates a noticeable learning curve. Players must quickly learn when to roll for mobility, when to transform back into mech form for maximum firepower, and how to navigate increasingly chaotic arenas filled with projectiles and environmental hazards. Early failures may be common, but each run provides valuable experience that gradually improves both mechanical skill and strategic decision-making. The challenge feels fair because success is earned through mastery rather than luck alone, making victories particularly satisfying. Go Mecha Ball succeeds by blending inventive movement mechanics with polished roguelite progression and exhilarating combat. Its seamless transformation system, highly interactive environments, impressive weapon variety, and rewarding customization create an experience that feels both accessible and mechanically deep. Rather than simply following trends established by other roguelites, it introduces fresh ideas that consistently keep players engaged from one run to the next. The combination of fast-paced action, creative level design, and meaningful replayability makes it an excellent choice for fans of arcade shooters and roguelite adventures alike. Rating: 8/10

I really don't need to recap how the gameplay works, because you can see it on the trailer and gameplay showcase videos. That's all there is to it. It's properly shown and telegraphed. The only gripe that i have is the same as i said in the first paragraph of this review before i added more : variety. It's technically a roguelike. You dead, you start from the beginning. But it lacks randomity that spice up other roguelike games. This goes for the main mode and arcade mode. Arcade mode is "random" because it shuffled the order of the main mode's levels, but it stays that way the whole time. So, no "true randomizer". The thing is, the levels are really well designed, but i think the devs can't decide whether to build a rogulike game or a traditional level-based game. The devs are working on other game(s) right now, so i understand that they won't update this game in a significant way. So here are my suggestions that (i think) does not require massive changes to the game : 1. Put some kind of randomizer in both modes (as basic as shuffling the order of the levels would be fine) 2. Technically speaking, there are 4 playable characters but as far as i know, the only differences between them are the stats (health and stuff) and one starting upgrade. At the very least make some of the abilities and/or upgrades exclusive to each of them. 3. Make a global leaderboard for the arcade mode (this might be cumbersome to implement though). And then boom, you will have a proper roguelike. TL;DR : Awesome gameplay, meh roguelike elements.
